Gastroenterology · published research

Atrophic gastritis

Summary of the Evidence

Two 2005 publications describe 633-nm helium-neon laser treatment in a chemically induced rat model of chronic atrophic gastritis. The overlapping authors, 63-animal design, induction method, three fluence groups, and 20-day schedule indicate that they are companion reports from one experiment rather than independent replications. One report adds cyclin-D1 findings (Shao et al. 2005; Yang et al. 2005).

Human and clinical evidence

No human PBM study for atrophic gastritis was identified. The available outcomes are gastric acid secretion and experimental tissue measures, not symptoms, endoscopic progression, gland recovery, or gastric-cancer risk.

Animal evidence

The experiment used a Wistar-rat model induced with sodium salicylate and alcohol alongside irregular fasting and forced exercise. At 3.36 J/cm², gastric acid secretion increased, the gastric mucosa was thicker, inflammatory-cell infiltration decreased, and parietal-cell morphology moved toward normal compared with untreated model controls. The companion report also described higher cyclin-D1 expression at this fluence. The 4.80- and 6.24-J/cm² groups did not show comparable improvement (Shao et al. 2005; Yang et al. 2005).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The two publications report a 633-nm helium-neon laser delivered once daily for 20 days at 3.36, 4.80, or 6.24 J/cm². The favorable findings occurred at the lowest tested fluence, indicating a fluence-specific response in this model rather than a simple dose-dependent improvement. The experiment does not establish tissue penetration, delivery, effectiveness, or safety for people.

Interpretation

The lowest tested fluence produced favorable gastric mucosal and acid-secretion findings in one rat experiment. Because the two publications appear to describe the same experiment and no independent animal replication or human study was identified, certainty remains very low and the findings do not establish a clinical effect on atrophic gastritis.

Publications and records

2 publications

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Very low for gastric mucosal structure and acid secretion in a rat model.

Rationale for the certainty assessment

Two 2005 publications appear to report one 63-rat experiment, with overlapping authors, induction methods, three fluence groups, and a 20-day schedule. Favorable gastric mucosal and acid-secretion findings occurred only at the lowest fluence and have not been independently replicated. No human evidence was identified, so certainty remains very low for these preclinical outcomes.

Publication and study types

1 animal experiment (rat; reported in 2 companion publications)
